page: Microsoft Azure E96d_v5 is an EDv5 family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 672.0 GB, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 3686 GB of local SSD storage and does not contain any GPUs.

Benchmark data shows strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also in the top 25% for both small-block cached reads at 5005.88 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 327.92 GB/sec. Cryptographic capabilities are notable, with the Passmark CPU encryption test reaching the top 10% tier, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and VAES instruction sets. Single-core performance benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, consistently rank in the middle 50%.

This server is configured for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and multi-threaded processing. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the top 25%, making it suitable for large-scale caching and relational databases. However, there are performance tradeoffs in large-scale machine learning; while prompt processing for a 135M LLM model is in the top 25%, text generation for a 70B model falls into the bottom 25% due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and local SSD storage provide qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high resource density without the expense of GPU accelerators.
description: Microsoft Azure E96d_v5 is an EDv5-series virtual machine featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 672.0 GB of RAM and 3686 GB of local SSD storage. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 server delivers strong multi-core performance and memory bandwidth, both ranking in the top 25% of benchmarks. Cryptographic execution is particularly efficient, placing in the top 10% due to hardware-accelerated instruction sets. While single-core benchmarks and large-scale LLM text generation show average to weak performance, the server excels in multi-threaded tasks, database operations, and high-throughput web serving. This hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive applications, relational databases, and caching systems that benefit from high local storage capacity and substantial memory density without requiring GPU acceleration.
